trust_decision.summary: pip decides that the file name derived from an index-supplied package URL is safe to join onto a directory: Link.filename must be percent-decoded exactly once and reduced to a single path component, and the three joins that write, copy or hash that name rely on it.

landing_point.why: The summary names a package URL but CWE-36 is a path-traversal file write; this is the only line where the URL-derived name becomes a filesystem path, so a summary-only engineer follows the write into Downloader.__call__.

fix_sites.entry_point: Link.filename, consumed by Downloader (pip install / pip download / pip wheel) and by every other filename caller
new _to_path_component / as_path_component / join_within_directory helpers exported from the model
Downloader.__call__ / batch public API (writes into the temp unpack directory)
get_http_url / get_file_url with a download dir (pip download -d), reuses or unlinks an existing file
RequirementPreparer.save_linked_requirement (pip download -d) copies the downloaded file into the download dir

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Link.filename reads as a display/metadata helper (it also feeds Wheel parsing and log lines), so a solver can argue the model must not carry filesystem policy and that guarding the download site alone is the real fix, leaving the second decode in the model.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Path-less URLs must keep falling back to the netloc (https://example.com/ -> example.com, asserted at tests/unit/test_link.py:39-45) and a double-encoded separator must stay a literal %2F in the name; an over-broad fix that rejects such names, or that rewrites sanitize_content_filename whose '../..' -> '..' result is asserted at tests/unit/test_network_download.py:141, breaks pinned tests.

O6_input_shapes: doubly-encoded separator in the path: https://example.com/a%252Fb.whl must give a%2Fb.whl (one decode, not a/b.whl)
doubly-encoded parent reference: https://example.com/%252e%252e%252fb.whl, and /foo/%2e%2e after the single decode
path that is only a . or .. segment: https://example.com/.. , https://example.com/. , https://example.com/foo/%2e%2e
path-less URL whose authority looks like a traversal: http://../ , http://..\..\..\evil.whl
content-disposition name that reduces to empty, . or .. (as_path_component rejects it instead of joining it)
a name carrying directory parts (nested/pkg.whl) reduced to its basename at the write site

O8b_injection_room.sibling: saving the VCS/editable archive (req.archive) into self.download_dir by name
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Same function and same destination directory as the fixed copy, reached through the other branch, so a maintainer writing a download-dir save would naturally join the name here too.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: copying the downloaded/built artefact into --wheel-dir by joining req.link.filename instead of taking the source basename
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It is the other CLI command that saves artefacts into a user-chosen directory, so the same name-join pattern belongs there.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: writing wheels next to a pylock by joining link.filename, mirrored by the reload join at src/pip/_internal/utils/pylock.py:162
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: link.filename is already persisted into the lock as the wheel/sdist name, and the reload route turns a stored relative path back into a URL by joining it onto the lock's directory.

O9_family: CWE-36 absolute path traversal (file name derived from a doubly-encoded URL used as a path inside a download directory)
